predecessors.name: Kushan Empire
predecessors.text: the eastern half of the Kushan realm: the Punjab, Taxila, the Doab and the Gangetic plain

successors.name: Gupta Empire
successors.text: the Punjab: 1,029 of the shape's 1,141 cells lie in Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 347

successors.name: Kidarites
successors.text: Peshawar and Gandhara, conquered by the Kidarites c.

ledger.x: 226: the eastern half of the Kushan realm becomes the Eastern Kushans.
240: Shapur I's Sasanians push east towards Gandhara.

c. 260: the Peshawar valley passes to the Sasanian-ruled Kushano-Sasanians. The page gives Shapur I's reign (240-270) for the advance into western Pakistan and Gandhara as the farthest point; 260 is Cliopatria's year, when its Indo-Sasanian row begins.

270: Shapur I's reign ends (240-270) with the Sasanians at the Indus; the page says they 'apparently did not cross the Indus River' and that coins of Sasanian type appear at Taxila only from Shapur II's reign.

c. 270: the Gangetic plain becomes independent of the Kushans. The Kushan Empire page says the territories on the Gangetic plain became independent around 270 and lists the Nagas of Padmavati and of Vindhyatabi among the empire's successors; its words are 'Around 270 their territories on the Gangetic plain became…

c. 270: Sindh, the southern Punjab and western Rajasthan pass to the Western Satraps in Cliopatria. No page opened for this state mentions it; the Kushan Empire page lists the Western Satraps only among the empire's predecessors, and the Western Satraps pages have Rudradaman holding…

c. 346: Samudragupta's Guptas absorb the Eastern Kushans' Punjab. The Kushan Empire page says Samudragupta subjugated the Eastern Kushans in the mid-4th century; the Allahabad pillar says the Kushan rulers offered 'self-surrender, offering (their own) daughters in marriage', and the Kushans kept their districts under…

wars.name: Shapur I's eastern campaign against the Kushans
wars.outcome: The Sasanians took the Kushan provinces of Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara and held them to the Indus; Shapur I's inscription claims Kushan territory as far as Purushapura.

wars.name: Samudragupta's subjugation of the Kushans
wars.outcome: The Kushan rulers sought the favour of Samudragupta, offering daughters in marriage and using the Garuda seal; they kept their districts as his subordinates.

certainty.note: The Punjab frontier with the Sasanians at the Indus and the Gangetic breakaway of c.
